clauses.mechanism: one_time_revocation_performed_on_stated_effective_date (own terms: effective on the thirtieth day from the date of the order)
clauses.reason: whole: The sole operative paragraph says the designations of Cordova, Alaska, and Mahukona, Hawaii, as customs ports of entry "are hereby revoked" and that the order becomes effective on "the thirtieth day from the date hereof". The order is dated November 5, 1942, so the thirtieth day from that date is December 5, 1942 (if the date hereof were counted as day one the day would be December 4; the words 'from the date hereof' count from the date). The revocation is a one-time command performed when it took effect, so the order is exhausted by performance on 1942-12-05 and the designations stay revoked as a surviving consequence. The order has no sunset, report or continuing duty.

research_rationale:
EO 9263 (signed November 5, 1942; 7 FR 9105; F.R. Doc. 42-11596, filed November 6, 1942) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. It has one operative paragraph, issued under section 1 of the act of August 1, 1914 (19 U.S.C. 2), that revokes the designations of Cordova, Alaska, and Mahukona, Hawaii, as customs ports of entry, followed by one sentence fixing the effective date at the thirtieth day from the date of the order. The revocation is a one-time self-executing command with no continuing duty, so it was performed, and the order exhausted, when it took effect on 1942-12-05 (the thirtieth day counted from November 5; November has 30 days). The revoked designations stay revoked as a surviving consequence (owner ruling 2026-10-28). The held page text also prints text of a neighboring order before this order's heading (character offsets before 2267, including a clause about Title I of the First War Powers Act); that text belongs to another order and was not used. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, transfer or exemption language. Its only lasting effect, that the designations of Cordova and Mahukona as customs ports of entry stand revoked, is an accrued consequence of the performed revocation; nothing continues as a command after 1942-12-05.
